## DG6 round 6 (T-DG6-REV-QA-RG-R6): verdict PASS on candidate `sha256:5e819f7a…35ed6`

The candidate is confirmed at the start and end of the run (2775 files, complete clone), and its product tree is identical to `60787d89f`. HEAD moved twice during the run, through delivery-record commits only: `c9eca6539` (orchestrator, `stages.json` state) and `aaef2cf47` (the domain reviewer's run evidence, which I did not read). Neither changes the candidate.

### Open findings: all three CLOSED_VERIFIED
- **F-DG6-911 and F-DG6-951 (Medium, the `stages.json` transition):** the `--historical` validators for DG5 through DG1, `--pipeline` and `--register DG6` all exit 0 now; in round 5 they exited 1. I served mutated copies of `stages.json` to the unchanged validator, in memory only:
  - removing the added FIXING entry brings back "illegal transition VERIFYING -> REVIEWING" (exit 1);
  - putting back the earlier state field fails the "state differs from last history entry" rule (exit 1);
  - the unmodified copy passes.
- **F-DG6-990 (Low, seeded text naming DG gates):** the auditor's round-4 probe now finds 0 served strings (it found 24). The shipped seeded-text scan passes 4/4.
  - Two mutants catch a revert: removing migration 0130 brings back the 24 strings; removing only its `kpi.freshness_scan` row leaves 2.
  - The rendered screens show 0 hits in English and Arabic (68 screens per language).
  - An SQL scan of every text column on both stacks finds no current value naming DG0-DG7.
  - I agree with D-239 on leaving the five audit reasons as append-only history.

### Full review results (all 19 checks PASS)

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Static checks | all 6 exit 0, both builds exit 0 |
| Unit tests, Node 22.22.0 and 24.21.0, both locale settings | exit 0 in all four runs |
| Integration, run twice | 442/442 files, 4370 passed; 122 migrations (0001–0130); 932 of 932 contract operations validated |
| `tests/qa` alone | 45 files / 437 tests, plus 6 / 61 unit |
| Product journeys, both locale settings | 556 passed each |
| Root acceptance specs, both locale settings | 288 passed each; axe found 0 violations on 108 screen states per language |
| Network capture (A21) | loopback connections only |
| Demo specs | 10/10 twice |
| Probes | all pass: 360/390 px and 200 % text, auditor read-only pass, XSS, keyboard walkthrough, restricted tokens, Arabic export literals |
| Worker burst | 126 jobs/s batched against 33 jobs/s unbatched; 0 duplicates |
| Load (provisional, one sandbox host) | worst p95 34.6 ms, 0 errors |

No test failed or timed out, so nothing needed a re-run. Every skip, todo, stderr line and non-zero exit is explained in the record:
- the 2 product skips are the keyboard-walkthrough spec, which needs the demo database; I ran it on the demo stack and it passes;
- the 18 root-spec skips are declared axe skips for screens whose records the scan doesn't create;
- the export proof exits 1 only on the LOAD-T20 dataset gap that the register already discloses;
- the mutant runs exit 1 by design.

**D-229 and D-228 (4):** neither is a defect. The token-sequence probe passes 5/5. Calls from another organization are refused on all 312 operations (403 or 404) and change no table.

### New finding
- **F-DG6-952 (Low, not mandatory, not blocking; owner delivery-orchestrator).** `stages.json` has out-of-order timestamps in two already-approved gates:
  - DG5's VERIFYING entry is dated 12:00Z, which is after its APPROVED entry (06:30Z) and after the commit that wrote it (04:34Z);
  - a DG0 round-28 REVIEWING entry is dated after the FIXING entry that follows it.

  The validator doesn't check time order. I proposed it for acceptance as an observation; that only takes effect if the release auditor co-signs.

### Observations (not findings)
- The demo connector's identity reason cites "ADR-0053 §1". It names an ADR, not a DG gate.
- Migration 0130 clears `updated_by` on a job row a user had changed; the user's change is still in the audit trail.

### Assignment problems
- It asks for `round: 3`, but the path is round 6 and the validator requires the record's round to match its directory. I used 6.
- Its literal repair diff (`3c8b9a3..3c8b9a3`) is empty, so I reviewed the real change since my round-3 PASS (`f56f1b3..3c8b9a3`: migration 0130, its scan test, the data dictionary).
- Node 22 is 22.22.0 on this host, not 22.22.2.

The Keycloak login spec and the SAML broker were not run (environmental residuals, recorded as the assignment directs). Cleaning up the leftover test temp directories in `$TMPDIR` was refused by the permission check; the runner deletes that directory when the run ends.

Records are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-6/`: `qa-verifier.json`, `qa-verifier.verifications.json` and `qa-verifier.findings.json`. The record and findings sidecar pass the repository's JSON schemas, and every evidence path exists. Evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/round-6/`; my new test helpers are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/tests/round-6/`. This is an engineering review only: it grants no business approval (G1–G6), and product G6 never implies DG7.
